title: A BI capture: what an operator's assistant saved from a signed-in browser or a vendor's MCP server
description: The manifest `capture_manifest.json` at the root of a capture folder. Two routes fill one: `browser` (the operator's assistant, in the operator's own signed-in browser, saves the BI tool's own downloads (definition files any installed reader already reads) and the values the tool shows (oracle files)) and `mcp` (the assistant calls the BI vendor's own MCP server and saves what its tools return in the same two roles); either way it lists the files here, and no stage calls a browser or an MCP server. What a route could not give (a report layout, a data source definition, the displayed values) is named in `gaps`, so the run says what it could not verify instead of staying silent. The core reads ONLY the files listed: `definitions` is what the run's reader parses; an `oracle` file is never parsed as a definition and never reaches a statement. Each file carries its SHA-256, so a file changed after the capture is refused. The `refused` list names, by code, every capture the tool or the identity did not allow, so a run that has nothing to read says why. Vendor-neutral: `tool` is the name of the installed reader that reads `definitions`, and `how` is the tool's own label for the action, as text.

route.description: How the files were obtained. `browser`: the operator's own signed-in browser session, driven by their assistant; no credential was handed to the agent. `mcp`: the BI vendor's own MCP server, called by the operator's assistant under the operator's sign-in; `server` names it. A file obtained another way says so in its own `route`.

tool.description: The installed BI reader (`metrics_agent.readers`) that reads `definitions`: the run's `bi_vendor`. Any string here; S0 checks it against the installed readers.

custody.description: Who held the data on its way to this folder. `customer` when the browser and the folder are the customer's own (their operator, their machine); `third-party` otherwise. A standalone run refuses a third-party capture.

captured_by.description: The identity the browser was signed in as: never a name, an email or a token. What it saw depends on it (row-level security, hidden fields, what it may download).

role.description: The identity's role on the container, as the tool names it (a workspace role, a site role).

row_filters_apply.description: Whether the tool's row-level security narrows what this identity sees; null when unknown. When true, an oracle value is this identity's number, not everyone's.

source.description: Where the capture came from, as the browser showed it. No query string: it can carry a session or a filter state.

definitions.description: The path, relative to the capture folder, of what the run's reader parses: one file (a downloaded report file) or one folder (a workbook beside the published data sources it uses). Every `definition` file lies at or under it.

rows_on_disk.description: Whether a definition file carries the tool's data rows (a report downloaded with its data, a packaged workbook with an extract). The reader never reads them; the operator is told before such a download.

refused.description: Every capture the tool or the identity did not allow, by code. A run whose `definitions` is missing is refused with these.

what.description: The capture that was attempted, in the tool's own words.

server.description: With route `mcp`: the MCP server the assistant called, as its `initialize` answer named it (`serverInfo`), and how it was reached. Never its credentials or its configuration.

read_only.description: Whether only read-only tools were enabled (the tool allow-list or the server's read-only mode).

gaps.description: What this capture does NOT hold that a full fetch would, one entry per kind: the run records each one and says what it therefore cannot verify. Empty or absent: nothing is missing.

path.description: Relative to the capture folder; never absolute, never above it.

role.description: `definition`: a file the reader parses. `oracle`: a value the tool showed, kept to check the agent's SQL against; never a definition.

how.description: The tool's action that produced it, in its own words: a menu path in the browser, the MCP tool's name (and the arguments that matter) over MCP.

format.description: An oracle file's layout. The encoding is read from its byte-order mark (UTF-8 or UTF-16).

header.description: Whether an oracle file's first line names its columns. A tool can leave it out for a single value.

formatted.description: Whether an oracle file's numbers are as DISPLAYED (thousands separators, rounded to the decimals shown), so a check rounds the agent's number to the same decimals; false when they are the tool's raw values.

route.description: How THIS file was obtained, when not by the manifest's `route`: a capture can mix routes (an MCP server that exposes no data source download, completed by the browser's download of it). `api`: the vendor's REST API under the operator's own credential. `file`: a file the operator already had.

widget.description: Which widget, and in which state, an oracle file holds, as the browser showed it.

sheet.description: The widget's own name where the tool shows one (a worksheet).

filters.description: The filters the tool listed on the widget when the values were taken (its filter pane), as shown. Empty: unfiltered.

refusal.description: content_not_visible: the identity cannot see the item. download_not_permitted: its role or a permission forbids the download. export_disabled: an admin setting turns the export off. label_export_blocked: a sensitivity label blocks it. rows_not_accepted: the only download carries data rows and the operator declined them. definitions_not_obtainable: no route gives this identity the definitions. no_machine_readable_oracle: the widget shows its values only as pixels. network_body_unavailable: the page's requests can be seen but not their bodies. session_expired: the operator must sign in again. download_incomplete: the file did not arrive whole. credential_prompt: the tool asked for a warehouse credential, which the assistant never types. write_refused: the only way on was an action that changes something. credential_reuse: the only way on was reusing the page's own token. tool_not_exposed: the MCP server has no tool that returns it. server_feature_off: an admin setting turns the MCP server (or that tool) off for this identity. terms_not_accepted: the server needs a licence the operator has not accepted; the assistant never accepts one for them. tool_error: an MCP tool answered with an error (its message, without any personal data, is the detail).

what.description: report_definition: no layout of the report or workbook (no widgets, pages, visual filters): questions come from the model alone. model_definition: no measure or calculation formulas. data_source_definition: a data source the definitions use is not in the capture (its tables and joins are unknown). displayed_values: no value the tool showed, so no widget can be checked against what a person sees. warehouse_lineage: the warehouse tables a data source reads are not named. row_security_context: the identity's row-level security cannot be told.

detail.description: Which objects, and why the route could not give them (for example: the server exposes no tool for it).

cannot_verify.description: What the run therefore cannot check, in words the run report repeats.

objects.description: The objects concerned, by the name the tool shows (a data source, a report).

access_code.description: When the gap is an access limit the route met (the BI tool's value service is off, a data source's embedded credentials are missing, a tool the server does not expose), its access_report code; the run records the gap as that blocker instead of a plain capture_gap.
